answer: An operator leases one numbered bay on a charted ropewalk and receives a sealed vial of yarrow distillate, mill-stamped to that bay alone. Only that holder may hang the inspection lantern on the bay hook, oil a single lay with that vial, and pull it while a side-door gale holds a published speed band. Graders match vial stamp, twist-shadow plate, wick coupon, and the door anemometer tape. A shared bay, leftover oil, or still-air pull is forfeited as one farm. Fielding N aliases costs N exclusive bays, N unique vials, and N live wind-band pulls no single walker can cover in the same hour.
